data.G: Pending research. At assembly, compare correctly validated measured candidates and combinations using the official end-to-end timing, then independently confirm the selected G. Preserve the fixed API, default stream, FP32 accuracy requirements, scratch bounds, and fresh-output semantics.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the source exposes three complementary opportunities, and the available time supports parallel research without inventing a fourth topic. The supplied baseline is correct and measured at 35.464 ms mean across three samples (35.441–35.485 ms); this is the combined timing, so it does not attribute time to individual kernels. In the current forward and input-gradient launches, L=48 gives one 256-thread block per (b,h) row, with only 48 threads producing outputs. The weight-gradient launch similarly has only 47 useful threads per block, and each output thread serially traverses B*L. These source-level observations motivate the three distinct objectives; their actual speedups remain unmeasured. All trees should compare complete calls with the official harness, validate every output against the required tolerances, and avoid assumptions that are valid only for the supplied performance dimensions. Scratch is uninitialized, so every read must follow a write in the same call.

children.objective: Own the separate forward and input-gradient kernels and their launch mapping in src/candidate.cu. Explore packing multiple short rows per CTA and other coalesced, well-utilized mappings to reduce inactive threads and CTA overhead; keep the two passes separate so this tree isolates mapping/kernel-efficiency gains from fusion. Preserve bounds-safe zero padding, full FP32, all-input correctness, complete output writes, and the fixed API. Judge candidates by correctness and full-call timing, not an assumed per-kernel benefit.
children.subject: Improve forward and input-gradient CTA mapping without fusion

children.objective: Own the forward/input-gradient execution path in src/candidate.cu. Test a fused kernel that computes y and gx together, sharing coordinate/filter handling where beneficial; measure whether fewer launches and shared work outweigh increased register use or reduced occupancy. Do not modify the weight-gradient path. Preserve full FP32, zero-padding semantics, all-input correctness and tolerances, complete fresh writes to both outputs, and the fixed API. Compare complete-call timing and report measured results rather than assuming fusion helps.
children.subject: Measure a fused forward and input-gradient kernel

children.objective: Own the weight-gradient kernel and its use of scratch in src/candidate.cu. Replace the long serial B*L accumulation per (h,j) with a parallel reduction, such as per-tile partial sums followed by a final reduction, using only supplied scratch and no extra allocations. Ensure every partial read is preceded by a write in the call, avoid accumulation across calls, and respect buffer bounds. Preserve the exact contracted gradient within the required FP32 tolerance and compare complete-call timing with correctness validation.
children.subject: Parallelize the weight-gradient reduction using scratch
